baseline_name: analytic standard error sigma/sqrt(n) of the gaussian at n=4096
best_variant: gaussian (RMSE x sqrt(n) / sigma at n=4096)

checks.check: gaussian: RMSE falls as 1/sqrt(n) (log-log slope in [-0.6, -0.4])
gaussian: every RMSE within [0.8, 1.25]x the analytic standard error
gaussian: no measured bias beyond four analytic bias standard errors
uniform: RMSE falls as 1/sqrt(n) (log-log slope in [-0.6, -0.4])
uniform: every RMSE within [0.8, 1.25]x the analytic standard error
uniform: no measured bias beyond four analytic bias standard errors

conclusion: hypothesis supported by all stated checks
falsifier: The fitted log-log slope of RMSE against n falls outside the stated band on either population, or any observed RMSE falls outside the stated multiple of the analytic standard error.
hypothesis: For the sample mean of independent draws from a population with known mean and finite variance, RMSE falls proportionally to 1/sqrt(n) (log-log slope in [-0.6, -0.4]) and observed RMSE stays within [0.8, 1.25]x the analytic standard error on a standard normal and a unit uniform population.
limitation: Synthetic Gaussian and uniform populations, sample mean only. The 1/sqrt(n) rate is a statement about independent draws from a fixed distribution with finite variance; it is not a measurement of any real quantity and says nothing about biased or dependent data.
method: 400 independent replications of the sample mean at each of n=[16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096] draws, per population; the true mean and sigma are known in closed form, so the error of every replication is exact rather than estimated.
metric: root-mean-square error of the sample mean

variants.name: gaussian (RMSE x sqrt(n) / sigma at n=4096)
